claim.claim_context: Active atomic proposition P-01 from the frozen ASA 25/261 Premium Grounding claim registry (origin F02/F04; type EXPLICIT; SUBJECTIVE; THERAPEUTIC; PRODUCT-SPECIFIC). Frozen evidence-preparation state: SOME DIRECT EVIDENCE LOCATED. Routing: STANDARD BIOMEDICAL ADJUDICATION
claim.claim_source_reference: INSPEKTORIUM Premium Grounding ASA 25/261 Final Evidence Freeze v1, sections 12/48; evidence cut-off 2026-08-22
claim.claim_text: Premium Grounding reduces aches and pain.
claim.intended_reader_or_audience: General consumer audience of a website health advertisement.

contradicting_or_limiting: H16 pain occurred in both groups; extreme multiplicity
H31 CK p=.534106; no CI, no MCID, no registration located
No chronic or condition-specific pain trial
Acute induced, occupational and postoperative models do not transfer to arthritis, back, neck or headache pain

evidence_items.text: Sokal et al. 2025: randomised, 42 active versus 42 sham ankle pads for one postoperative night with paracetamol for all. VAS mean change 2.50 versus 1.5952, exact p=.010511. Table 2 medians 2.5 versus 1; narrative and abstract give 2.0 versus 1.
evidence_items.why_it_matters: The strongest direct human efficacy signal located. The exact p-value is .010511 — significant at the .05 level, NOT at .01. Summary statistics conflict across the paper.

evidence_items.text: Brown, Chevalier & Hill 2015 (randomised double-blind, 16 active/16 sham) and Chevalier et al. 2019 (16 massage therapists) report pain and soreness signals.
evidence_items.why_it_matters: Induced-soreness and occupational contexts; H22 shares its cohort with H21.

evidence_items.text: Brown, Chevalier & Hill 2015 reported pain occurring in both groups, with isolated biomarker differences among many outcomes and timepoints.
evidence_items.why_it_matters: The induced-soreness line does not show a clean pain benefit.

evidence_items.text: Sokal et al. 2025 CK mean change 54.619 versus 40.5 U/L, p=.534106 — not significantly different between groups.
evidence_items.why_it_matters: The muscle-damage biomarker in the same trial showed no group difference, so a coherent mechanistic story is not established.

evidence_items.text: No condition-specific chronic-pain RCT with a minimal clinically important difference, medication use and follow-up was located; no registration was located for H31.
evidence_items.why_it_matters: The advertised chronic-pain framing has no supporting trial, and the strongest study lacks prespecification.

evidence.evidence_sufficiency_rationale: Sufficient for a bounded acute-context statement; insufficient for the advertised general and chronic pain claim.
supporting: H31 postoperative VAS, exact p=.010511 (randomised, sham, n=84)

detected.rationale: Evidence from one postoperative night, induced muscle soreness in healthy young men and 16 massage therapists is extended to general and chronic pain across four named conditions.
An unqualified pain-reduction benefit is advertised from a single significant acute result that reports no confidence interval and no clinical-relevance threshold.

reader_impact.affected_decision_type: Chronic pain management and care seeking.
reader_impact.likely_reader_misunderstanding: That a demonstrated acute postoperative effect means the product treats their chronic pain.
reader_impact.risk_rationale: Pain is the second advertised benefit and is paired with chronic conditions; readers may defer treatment.

recommended_revision.rewrite_rationale: Out of scope for RUN 001: this run adjudicates the frozen wording only. Replacement claim language occurs downstream after verdict freeze.

uncertainty.alternative_label_rationale: A solid reading was seriously considered and is recorded as the documented alternative: H31 is the strongest direct efficacy signal in the substrate. It is rejected as primary because the advertised wording is unqualified and sits beside a list of chronic conditions none of the evidence addresses.
uncertainty.ambiguity: MATERIAL AND DECISIVE — the Steelman layer established genuine bounded efficacy evidence while the adversarial layer established that the advertised framing is far broader than that evidence. Resolved as QUALIFIED: supported within documented acute bounds, not supported as advertised.
missing_evidence: H16 pain occurred in both groups; extreme multiplicity
H31 CK p=.534106; no CI, no MCID, no registration located
No chronic or condition-specific pain trial
Acute induced, occupational and postoperative models do not transfer to arthritis, back, neck or headache pain
scope_limitations: Adjudication is bounded to the frozen evidence substrate at the 2026-08-22 cut-off. No new literature discovery was performed.
The ASA regulatory outcome is quarantined and contributes no scientific inference.
unresolved_questions: Clinical relevance of the H31 effect is unknown without a CI or MCID; no chronic-pain trial exists.

verdict.verdict_summary: This is the advertised outcome with the strongest direct human evidence: a randomised sham-controlled trial in 84 post-lumbar-surgery patients found a VAS mean change of 2.50 versus 1.5952, exact p=.010511. That supports a bounded conclusion in acute induced, occupational and postoperative contexts only. It does not support the broad chronic-pain framing the advertisement uses, and the trial reports no confidence interval and no formal minimal clinically important difference.
